claims.text: The trip's own GPS trace measures 23.97 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal of 18.00 km — an excess of 5.97 km, or 33.17% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 gates pass: the excess is greater than 20% of optimal (3.60 km) and greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. The route deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's evidence.

POL-RD-01 makes the trace polyline the governing measurement, and I cite it: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 23.97 km and governs over the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km of 24.00 km. The threshold finding does not rest on the convenience copy, so it cannot be displaced by it.

The trace is clean for policy purposes and the deviation may therefore be established on it alone: 241 fixes at a 10-second interval with 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0 seconds — nowhere near POL-RD-07's 90-second gap or 500 m jump limbs, and well under its 30-second sustained-interval limb. No independent corroboration is required.

The rider's POL-RD-08 burden is discharged on the face of the artifacts: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00114, the pickup window matches (trip started_at 18:40:00, trace first fix 18:40:00), and the measured excess clears the POL-RD-01 threshold. The burden now shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause to excuse the excess.

The rider's own profile does not raise the corroboration bar under POL-RD-08: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, far below the 4-or-more trigger, and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1. This claim needs nothing beyond the trace it already has.

The driver's explanation — 'AYE was crawling from the Alexandra exit' — is, under POL-RD-13, tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. The only advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00114-01, is MISSING: it has no payload and weight_multiplier 0.0. I disclose that impairment and cite the artifact for its absence, not its content. With no advisory record, POL-RD-03's comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the congestion assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08.

The absent advisory is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation. The driver names no evidence ID for any advisory — his statement says only 'No advisory that I know of'. Under POL-RD-13(1) an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one, so this is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact. POL-RD-10(5) does not fire, and the case should be ruled on rather than escalated.

POL-RD-13(2) then fixes the consequence: where the rider has shown an excess meeting POL-RD-01 on a trace that is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) — as here — the deviation stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route. The driver's traffic assertion neither reduces the excess nor supplies an amended optimal.

No rider instruction caused this detour, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable to the driver. The chat log holds exactly two messages: the rider asking 'adam road?? jurong is the other way' at 18:58:40 and the driver answering 'AYE jam boss, this way faster' at 18:59:20. Neither is a rider instruction to take a particular road, and both message waypoint_hint fields are null.

The driver's own words corroborate his deliberate departure from the optimal corridor. He wrote 'this way faster' at 18:59:20, after the off-optimal Adam Road gantry was already charged at 18:57:12, and his filed statement concedes he 'went up and over on the PIE'. That is a driver admission in the chat log of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) names as an independent source, and it means the finding would stand even if the trace were impaired — which it is not.

With the deviation established and no exculpatory clause available, POL-RD-02 fixes the refund arithmetically because fare_model is METERED: ((3.80 + 0.75 x 18.00 + 0.28 x 30.00) x 1.6) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 ERP on the optimal route = 44.42. Charged total is 58.10, so the refund is 13.68, rounded up to SGD 13.70.

The 1.6 surge multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, where POL-RD-02 says it lives, and the rider does not contest it. It is applied to the recomputed base, distance and time charges (25.70 x 1.6 = 41.12) and not to ERP. The refund therefore does not claw back any of the surge the rider accepted.

The $2.00 Adam Road gantry is off the optimal corridor (on_optimal_route false), but I do not ask for it on top of the refund. Under POL-RD-09(1) it is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 figure, because the recomputed fare includes only the $2.50 Kim Keat Link gantry that lies on the optimal route. It is itemised for transparency and must never be added twice.

Neither billed gantry is a phantom line, and the rider does not assert a POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity correction: the trace passes within 0.0 m of the PIE (Kim Keat Link) gantry and within 8.76 m of the PIE (Adam Rd) gantry, both inside the 250 m match radius. The off-route ERP is a genuine crossing, not a charge line the trace never touches.

The refund of 13.68 is 23.5% of the 58.10 charged, below the 90% full-refund share POL-RD-02 sets, and it is above the 0.50 de minimis floor. The correct outcome for the filing rider is therefore PARTIAL_REFUND of the contested charge, not FULL_REFUND.

I do not press the POL-RD-06 uplift, because the record does not support it: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1, below the 3-or-more gate, and 1 over 412 completed trips is a ratio of 0.002, far below the 0.05 gate. Nor is this a MATERIAL deviation — the excess is 33.17%, under the 50% gate, and 5.97 km, under the 8.0 km gate — so no conduct referral arises under POL-RD-06(c). The rider's remedy is the POL-RD-02 partial refund and nothing further.

No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires. The trace is not impaired, all three artifacts carry trip_id TRP-00114, no exculpatory clause has been invoked against a cited artifact, both billed gantry lines are matched to the trace, no two admitted artifacts disagree by more than 10 minutes, and the refund of 13.68 is far below the 150.00 ceiling and below charged_total. This case is ripe for a monetary ruling, not a hold.

claims.text: Measured from the field the policy names — gps_trace.trace_distance_km of 23.97 km, not the rounded 24.0 km convenience copy on the trip record — the excess over the booked optimal of 18.0 km is 5.97 km, or 33.17%. That clears the establishment gate in POL-RD-01 (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km; both tests pass on the trace figure), but it falls well short of the materiality gate: the excess is neither greater than 50% of the optimal distance nor greater than 8.0 km absolute. This is an established but ordinary deviation, and the materiality consequences do not attach.

Because the deviation is not material, POL-RD-06 is not engaged: there is no basis for the FULL_REFUND uplift in limb (b) of that clause and none for the driver-conduct referral in limb (c). Even if the profile check is run, no pattern is established on the only two counters POL-RD-06 and POL-GEN-01 permit: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1, below the threshold of 3, and 1 divided by completed_trips_90d of 412 is 0.0024, far below the 0.05 ratio. Limbs (a) to (c) all fail.

The recomputation runs on the multiplier recorded on the fare breakdown, and fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier is 1.6 — a figure the rider expressly accepts in the claim. Surge applies to the base, distance and time lines only: (3.80 + 0.75 x 18.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x 1.6 = 41.12, plus the 0.80 platform fee and the 2.50 Kim Keat Link gantry that lies on the optimal route, giving a recomputed fare of 44.42. The surge uplift is therefore properly part of the comparison figure and is not stripped out of it.

The rider's "$4.50 of ERP" is not a sum that can be refunded on top of the recomputation. Only the 2.00 charged at the PIE (Adam Rd towards Tuas) gantry sits off the optimal route; the 2.50 at PIE (Kim Keat Link) carries on_optimal_route true and is properly chargeable, and it is already carried inside the 44.42 recomputed fare. The off-route 2.00 is itself already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund, because the recomputed fare includes only gantries lying on the optimal route — adding it again would double-count it, which POL-RD-09(1) expressly forbids. POL-RD-09(2) does not open a separate pass-through refund here because nothing is exonerated under POL-RD-03.

Neither billed gantry is a phantom line, so no standalone billing-integrity refund arises under POL-RD-09(4). The trace passes within 0 m of the Kim Keat Link gantry and within 8.76 m of the Adam Rd gantry — both far inside the 250 m match the clause applies — and no airport surcharge appears anywhere on this trip. The two artifacts carrying this are COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so no admissibility discount applies to the finding.

The arithmetic therefore lands at a refund of 13.68, rounded up to 13.70: charged_total of 58.10 less recomputed_fare of 44.42. That is not de minimis — it is well above the 0.50 floor under POL-RD-02 — and it is 23.5% of charged_total, far below the 90% share at which a partial converts to a full refund. The outcome the policy produces is a PARTIAL_REFUND of 13.70 against the 15.00 contested, on the separate lines charged_total 58.10, recomputed_fare 44.42, refund 13.70.

The driver's congestion explanation cannot be certified on this record and I do not press it as an exoneration. The bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00114-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so the POL-RD-03 comparison — a named segment the optimal route traverses, an overlapping validity window, and a route leaving and rejoining the corridor — cannot be run at all, and under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13 a congestion assertion naming no advisory carries no weight and supplies no adjusted optimal. No other exculpatory limb is open either: the chat log records a rider query, not a rider instruction, and carries no waypoint_hint (POL-RD-04); no pickup or dropoff amendment exists (POL-RD-05); the fare model is METERED, not UPFRONT_QUOTE (POL-RD-11); and the vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL (POL-RD-12). The deviation stands at the measured figure and the case is decided on the arithmetic.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: your route-deviation claim is upheld in part. The trip's GPS trace measures 23.97 km between the recorded pickup (Bugis Junction) and dropoff (Jurong East MRT) against the booked optimal of 18.00 km — an excess of 5.97 km, or 33.17% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km), so the deviation is established. It is not a MATERIAL deviation, however: the excess is neither above 50% of optimal nor above 8.0 km, so the POL-RD-06 full-refund uplift and the driver-conduct referral do not arise.

To the driver: the detour is not excused. You explained that the AYE was crawling and you went up and over the PIE, but no traffic advisory is on file for this trip — EV-ADVIS-00114-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run and, under POL-RD-13, the congestion assertion carries no weight. Because no advisory evidence ID was cited, this is a gap in the bundle and not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation; the case is ruled rather than held. No rider instruction caused the detour (POL-RD-04 — the chat holds only a rider query, no waypoint_hint), there was no pickup/dropoff amendment (POL-RD-05), the fare model is METERED not upfront (POL-RD-11), and the vehicle is RYDE_X not a pooled trip (POL-RD-12). The deviation stands at the measured figure.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02. Because the fare model is METERED, the recomputed fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 × 18.00 + 0.28 × 30.00) × 1.6) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 ERP on the optimal route = 44.42. The 1.6 surge multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and applied only to base, distance and time; the rider accepts it, so none of it is clawed back. Charged total is 58.10, so the refund is 58.10 − 44.42 = 13.68, rounded up to SGD 13.70.

On ERP: the 2.50 PIE (Kim Keat Link) gantry lies on the optimal route and remains inside the recomputed fare. The 2.00 PIE (Adam Rd) gantry is off the optimal route but is already comprehended in the refund, so it is itemised for transparency and not added again (POL-RD-09(1)). Neither gantry is phantom (the trace passes within 0 m and 8.76 m of them, inside the 250 m match), and there is no airport surcharge, so no billing-integrity correction arises.

The refund is 23.5% of the charged total — below the 90% full-refund share — and above the 0.50 de minimis floor, so a partial refund of the 15.00 contested is the correct outcome. Confidence rests on artifacts all at weight 1.0: the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00114), the trip record (EV-TRIP-00114) and the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00114).

ruling.explanation:
Rider — your Bugis–Jurong East trip of 7 August 2026, billed at $58.10, is partly refunded. The route deviation is confirmed on the trip's own evidence: the GPS trace measures 23.97 km against the booked optimal route of 18.00 km, an excess of 5.97 km, or 33.17%. That clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gate (more than 20% of optimal and more than 0.8 km absolute), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. It is not a MATERIAL deviation, because 33.17% is below the 50% gate and 5.97 km is below the 8.0 km gate.

Driver — your explanation that the AYE was crawling and you went up and over on the PIE is not certified on this record. There is no traffic advisory on file for this trip: EV-ADVIS-00114-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. With no advisory, the POL-RD-03 comparison (a named segment the optimal route traverses, an overlapping validity window, and a route leaving and rejoining the corridor) cannot be run; under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13 your uncited congestion assertion carries no weight and supplies no adjusted optimal route. This does not escalate the case: you named no advisory evidence ID (your statement says 'No advisory that I know of'), so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged, and POL-RD-13(1) directs that the case be decided on the arithmetic. No other exculpatory limb is open — the chat log records a rider query and your reply 'AYE jam boss, this way faster', but no rider instruction to take a particular road and no waypoint (POL-RD-04); no pickup or dropoff was amended (POL-RD-05); the fare is METERED, not upfront (POL-RD-11); and the vehicle is RYDE_X, not a pooled trip (POL-RD-12).

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, run on the fare breakdown: base $3.80 + distance (0.75 × 18.00 km = $13.50) + time (0.28 × 30.00 min = $8.40) = $25.70, multiplied by the 1.6 surge you both accept ($41.12), plus the $0.80 platform fee and the $2.50 Kim Keat Link gantry that lies on the optimal route = recomputed_fare $44.42. Charged total was $58.10. On the separate lines the ruling rests on: charged_total $58.10, recomputed_fare $44.42, refund $13.68, rounded up to $13.70. That is above the $0.50 de minimis floor and 23.5% of the charge, far below the 90% share that would convert this to a full refund.

On the ERP: only the $2.50 Kim Keat Link gantry lies on the optimal route. The $2.00 Adam Road gantry is off-route, but it is already comprehended in the $44.42 recomputed fare and must not be added on top (POL-RD-09(1)); it is itemised here for transparency only. Both gantries are genuine crossings — the trace passes within 0.0 m and 8.76 m of them, inside the 250 m match — so there is no phantom line, no billing-integrity correction and no referral under POL-RD-09(4).

POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no driver-conduct referral arises: this deviation is not material, and in any event no repeat pattern is established on the only citable counters — driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 (below 3) and 1 over 412 completed trips is 0.002 (below 0.05). The refund is well below the $150.00 escalation ceiling. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: confidence is above the 0.70 floor, all three artifacts carry trip_id TRP-00114, the trace is unimpaired (241 fixes, 10-second interval, zero gaps), the timestamps agree, and every billed line has a counterpart in the trace.

ruling.explanation:
This ruling concerns trip TRP-00114 (Friday 7 August 2026, Bugis Junction to Jurong East MRT).

Deviation. The booked optimal distance is 18.00 km. The GPS trace — the governing measurement under POL-RD-01 — is 23.97 km; the trip record's rounded 24.00 km is a convenience copy and was not used for the threshold test. The excess is 5.97 km, or 33.17% of optimal, so both POL-RD-01 establishment gates pass (over 20% and over 0.8 km) and the deviation is ESTABLISHED. It is not MATERIAL: 33.17% is under 50% and 5.97 km is under 8.0 km, so the POL-RD-06 profile check does not fire and no FULL_REFUND uplift or driver-conduct referral arises. That is confirmed on the record: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 (under the 3 gate) and 1/412 = 0.002 (under the 0.05 ratio gate). driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter that POL-GEN-01 makes context only, and it was not used.

Trace integrity. The trace is clean under POL-RD-07(a)–(c): 241 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds. It is not impaired, so no independent corroboration is required to establish the deviation; the driver's chat message ('this way faster') and his filed statement are noted but not needed.

Driver's excuse. The driver attributes the route to AYE congestion. POL-RD-13 requires that assertion to be tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. The bundle's only advisory, EV-ADVIS-00114-01, is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. It neither reduces the excess nor supplies an adjusted optimal. Because the driver named no advisory identifier, POL-RD-13(1) applies: this is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) does not fire and the case is ruled rather than escalated. No other exculpatory limb is open: there is no rider instruction in the chat log (both waypoint_hint fields are null), so POL-RD-04 is unavailable; there is no pickup or dropoff amendment, so POL-RD-05 is unavailable; the fare model is METERED, not UPFRONT_QUOTE (POL-RD-11); and the vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL (POL-RD-12).

Fare. Under POL-RD-02 (METERED): recomputed fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 18.00 + 0.28 x 30.00) x 1.6 + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 ERP on the optimal route = 44.42. The 1.6 surge multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, applies to base, distance and time only, and is not applied to ERP. Charged total is 58.10. Refund = 58.10 - 44.42 = 13.68, rounded up to SGD 13.70. The off-route ERP of 2.00 (PIE Adam Rd gantry) is already comprehended in this figure, because the recomputed fare includes only the on-optimal-route 2.50 Kim Keat Link gantry; under POL-RD-09(1) it must never be added again. Both billed gantries were genuinely crossed (trace within 0 m and 8.76 m of them), so no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity correction and no referral arises. The refund is above the 0.50 de minimis floor and is 23.5% of the charged total, below the 90% share, so it is a partial refund, not a full one.

Confidence. Every artifact that carries a deciding fact — the GPS trace and trip record for the excess, the fare breakdown and trip record for the arithmetic — is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0 and no admissibility discount applies. No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires.

Outcome: the rider is refunded SGD 13.70 of the disputed charge.
